title: M-C Terrain Pressure (Chomp Spine)
lede: Garchomp-centered M-C six: Primarina + Gholdengo as the balance spine, Rillaboom + Sneasler + Mimikyu as flex. Preview names the Speed story — Mega/Scarf/Sash Chomp, Grassy Glide, or Unburden — then brings the two partners that cash it.
philosophy: Same Garchomp three-mode spine as the Golisopod/Salamence manual, but the flex wins are terrain offense and Unburden races — not First Impression or double-stone Mega ambiguity. Meta foundation + two disrupting axes.
meta: Season M-6 Singles (as of 2026-09-16, Champions Battle Data): Salamence #1, Garchomp #2, Primarina #3, Golisopod #5, Archaludon #8, Gholdengo #9, Rillaboom #10, Mimikyu #11, Sneasler #18. Regulation M-C legalized Garchompite Z; this six registers only that stone. Rillaboom’s CBD teammates already include Primarina and Garchomp — the construction is a re-weight of flex, not an invented core.
setsNote: 66 SP, max 32. Default roster Garchomp is Mega teaching mode (Garchompite Z). Scarf and Sash are first-class preview modes. Rillaboom defaults Life Orb; swap Grassy Seed when you want bulk and a Seed pop for Sneasler Unburden. Sneasler defaults Grassy Seed on this six — Psychic Seed / Gem / Sash when Boom is not on the three.

evidence.caveat: Construction evidence from Singles CBD — not VGC doubles cores. Early season; treat as teachable structure, not proven best WR.

stats.label: Garchompite Z
stats.note: Largest Chomp item mode — Mega breaker is real, not mandatory.

stats.label: Rillaboom Grassy Glide
stats.note: Near-universal. Priority under terrain is the lever.

stats.label: Sneasler Unburden
stats.note: Psychic Seed leads ladder items; this six prefers Grassy Seed with Boom.

stats.label: Sneasler Close Combat
stats.note: Dire Claw and Swords Dance follow — Fighting pressure is the job.

stats.label: Mimikyu Life Orb
stats.note: Play Rough ~97% — Disguise into Fairy STAB / Shadow Sneak.

stats.label: Top Boom mates
stats.note: Then Lucario, Hippowdon, Golisopod. Spine already exists on ladder.

construction.thesis: Start with Garchomp + Primarina + Gholdengo, then hold Rillaboom, Sneasler, and Mimikyu so Mega, Scarf, and Sash Chomp all have partners — and so the six can attack Water/Ground density and Steel sits without Golisopod or Salamence.
construction.method: Keep the proven balance triangle. Replace Golisopod’s priority finisher job with Grassy Glide and Mimikyu Shadow Sneak. Replace Salamence’s alt Mega / Dance with Unburden Sneasler as the second Speed story. Skip auto-adding Baxcalibur (Dragon overlap + Fairy hole) and skip forcing Archaludon into a rain story.
construction.winCondition: Preview → name the Speed story (Mega break / Scarf revenge / Glide race / Unburden race) → pick Chomp’s item if Chomp is in → bring the two partners that cash that story.

substitutions.why: Golisopod is #5 and a real mate, but this six wants anti-Water/Ground pressure and terrain as a lever. Glide fills the priority-finisher class with different typing.
Salamence gives Mega ambiguity; this manual accepts a single stone so Unburden can be the second Speed axis without competing for Mega.

altSlots.why: When you want First Impression / Emergency Exit over Disguise into a specific HO.
When you want double-stone Mega ambiguity back — use the Three-Mode Chomp manual instead.
Fast Dark/Grass pivot when Unburden Seed lines feel wrong and you still need anti-Water Speed.

megaPool.rule: One Mega per battle. This six registers Garchompite Z only — Scarf or Sash Garchomp is an intentional tell that the stone is off.
megaPool.previewPressure: They see Garchomp and must still guess Mega / Scarf / Sash. The new preview question is which Speed story is live: Chomp mode, Boom Glide, or Sneasler Unburden.

candidates.when: Their six is Ground-weak, Fairy is answered on the three, and Mega breaker beats Scarf revenge or a Boom/Sneasler race.

pilot.thesis: Name the Speed story before the lead. Chomp’s item is a preview decision equal to the three; Boom and Sneasler exist so Glide and Unburden can be the win without locking Chomp to Scarf every game.
pilot.rule: One primary Speed story per game — Mega break, Scarf revenge, Glide race, or Unburden race.
pilot.fail: Auto-bring Chomp / Primarina / Gholdengo into fat Water, or Grassy Seed Sneasler without Boom on the three.

press: Force them to respect Mega, Scarf, and Sash Garchomp from the same registered name.
Use Rillaboom to attack Primarina / Hippo / Ground-heavy structures the balance spine struggles with.
Use Sneasler so Chomp does not have to be Scarf every Speed-critical game.
Use Primarina Encore to create SD / Unburden / Disguise windows.
refuse: Never treat Stealth Rock as mandatory.
Never Mega Chomp into healthy Fairy without Gholdengo on the three.
Never leave Primarina home vs Mega Salamence.
Never soft Grassy Glide into Fire / Flying resists.
Never lead Unburden into known priority Dark without Mimikyu or Primarina backup.

plan.title: Preview
plan.goal: Decide the Speed story and Chomp’s mode if Chomp is in.
plan.play: Mark Water/Ground density, Fairy answers, HO shape, Steel sits, and Mega Salamence. Assign Mega / Scarf / Sash / leave-Chomp, then pick Boom, Sneasler, or Mimikyu.
plan.next: Lead the partner that enables that story — not the partner you practiced most.

plan.title: Pressure
plan.goal: Put something into KO range for Glide, Shadow Sneak, Aqua Jet, or the Mega breaker.
plan.play: EQ / coverage from Chomp, Knock / Glide from Boom, Encore from Primarina, Plot from Gholdengo, Unburden SD from Sneasler, Disguise from Mimikyu.
plan.next: If the Speed story was wrong, change item or pack next game — keep the six.

plan.title: Close
plan.goal: Convert chip without donating the wincon to Fairy, Ice, or priority Dark.
plan.play: Gholdengo holds Fairy; Primarina handles Dragons; Boom Glides; Mimikyu Sneaks; Scarf Chomp cleans.
plan.next: Mega breaks; Scarf cleans; Sash already spent — don’t ask it to wall; Unburden is glass after the pop.

switches.send: Gholdengo — Steel resists; Make It Rain answers.
Garchomp — Ground immunity and pressure (Boom if Chomp benched).
Rillaboom — Knock Off or Grassy Glide.

victims.name: Electric / Steel midrange
victims.why: Ground STAB plus Primarina Fairy forces awkward switches; Sneasler cracks leftover Steel.

victims.name: Water / Ground fat
victims.why: Boom Glide and Knock attack the sits that stall EQ.

victims.name: Glass HO
victims.why: Mimikyu Disguise plus Glide / Jet / Sneak deny free turns.

victims.name: Physical Balance without Fairy
victims.why: Mega or Scarf Chomp + Gholdengo Plot outlasts one wall.

counters.name: Double Fairy + Ice
counters.why: Chomp and Sneasler both suffer — lean Gholdengo/Primarina/Boom and Scarf revenge over Mega SD.

counters.name: Mega Salamence + Ice backup
counters.why: Primarina + Gholdengo mandatory; leave Chomp often.

counters.name: Priority Dark into Mimikyu / Unburden
counters.why: Disguise and Seed pops are not immortality — don’t lead them into known Sucker / First Impression Dark.

advantages.title: Three Speed stories
advantages.body: Mega/Scarf/Sash Chomp, Grassy Glide, and Unburden are incompatible answers from one registered six. Exploit that before the lead drops.

advantages.title: Terrain as a lever
advantages.body: Boom is not a dedicated Grassy archetype chapter. Fake Out / Glide / Knock pressure Water and Ground; Seed can enable Sneasler when both are registered.
advantages.play: Bring Boom when Water/Ground density is the problem — not every game.

advantages.title: Hazards optional
advantages.body: Earthquake is the Chomp constant. Stealth Rock is a package tool for Mimikyu/Glide chip — skip when the three needs coverage.
advantages.play: Sash lead Rocks is a mode, not a religion.

flows.title: Preview
flows.lede: Name the Speed story, then the three.

forks.when: Mega Salamence or strong Ice + Fairy on their six.
forks.then: Bring Primarina + Gholdengo + Boom or Sneasler. Leave Chomp often; if Chomp, Scarf only.
forks.why: Moonblast / Fairy net first. Ground Dance into Aerilate Flying is a bad story.

forks.when: Water / Ground fat — Primarina, Hippowdon, Chomp mirrors.
forks.then: Bring Rillaboom + Primarina + Chomp Mega or Gholdengo.
forks.why: Glide and Knock are the levers the balance spine lacks.
Close Combat and Knock crack sits EQ alone stalls on.

forks.then: Bring Mimikyu + Primarina + Boom or Sneasler. Chomp Sash only if you need a guaranteed action.
forks.why: Disguise and priority deny free turns — not Mega Chomp lead.

forks.when: Need max Speed pressure and accept less glue.
forks.why: Offense over glue — refuse Fairy + priority Dark stacks.

loops.title: Encore → SD / Unburden
loops.body: Primarina Encores Protect or setup; Mega Chomp or Sneasler converts the free turn.

loops.title: Knock → Glide
loops.body: Boom strips Sitrus / Leftovers / Balloon; Grassy Glide finishes the chipped Water or Ground.

loops.title: Chip → Shadow Sneak / Aqua Jet
loops.body: Chomp or Boom puts a name in range; Mimikyu or Primarina priority closes.

loops.title: Disguise → Scarf clean
loops.body: Mimikyu eats one hit; Scarf Chomp revenge the switch or the weakened attacker.

loops.title: Seed pop → Unburden SD
loops.body: Grassy Seed (or Psychic Seed) pops; Sneasler Swords Dance or immediately Close Combats.

hazards.title: Fairy on Chomp
hazards.body: Dragon/Ground hates Fairy. Gholdengo is the registered answer — if it is not on the three, do not force Mega Chomp into Moonblast.
hazards.rule: No Fairy answer on the three → different pack or Scarf revenge from a safer slot.

hazards.title: Grassy Seed without Boom
hazards.body: Sneasler’s Team A default is Grassy Seed because Boom sets terrain. On packs without Boom, swap Psychic Seed, Normal Gem, or Focus Sash.
hazards.rule: Item must match the three — not the registered six fantasy.

hazards.title: Ice into Dragons / Unburden
hazards.body: Chomp shares Ice pain with many Dragons; Sneasler hates Ice priority after the Seed pop. Primarina and Mimikyu are insurance.
hazards.watch: Choice Scarf Ice and priority Ice.

itemAlts.why: Second ladder identity — revenge and Speed control when Mega is wrong or Boom/Sneasler need the setup turn.

itemAlts.name: Focus Sash
itemAlts.why: Third ladder identity — guarantee Rocks or a hit into HO / revenge.

training.label: Fast physical Mega

alts.name: Mixed / special lean

roster.objective: Break, revenge, or guarantee a lead action — pick one before the timer ends.
roster.howToPlay:
On preview, assign Mega, Scarf, Sash, or leave home.
Do not default Stealth Rock — only when the package wants chip for Mimikyu/Glide.
If Fairy is healthy and Gholdengo is benched, you picked the wrong three.
Vs Mega Salamence, Scarf revenge or leave — not Mega Dance.

modes.when: Their six is Ground-vulnerable, Fairy is answered, and Mega breaker beats a Glide or Unburden race.
modes.objective: Crack the defensive structure; do not play like a hazard lead.
modes.howToPlay:
Mega when the breaker job is clear.
SD only after Encore, Disguise, or a forced switch.
Mixed sets swap coverage for Draco / Earth Power / Flamethrower when their walls are physical.

modes.when: Need revenge vs Mega Salamence / Unburden / fast special, or Boom/Mimikyu create chip while you clean.

moves.name: Outrage
moves.why: Dragon nuke when you accept the lock — Dragon Claw if you need flexibility.

modes.objective: Be the fast answer after chip — not the lead setup piece.
modes.howToPlay:
Bring when Speed tiers scare you.
Do not lead Scarf into known resist walls.
Pair with Primarina/Boom/Mimikyu so something else creates the chip.

modes.label: Focus Sash
modes.when: You need Rocks, a trade, or a hit into something that would otherwise OHKO — and Glide or Shadow Sneak finishes.
modes.itemWhy: Clear #3 ladder identity. Guarantees Garchomp does its job once.

training.label: Sash utility
training.why: Offense first — Sash is the bulk.

moves.name: Stealth Rock
moves.why: Chip for Mimikyu / Glide finishes — skip if you needed coverage.

modes.objective: Guarantee something happens on the lead turn.
modes.howToPlay:
Lead when HO or revenge would delete un-Sashed Chomp.
After Sash breaks, you are glass — hand off to Boom or Mimikyu.

itemAlts.name: Leftovers

roster.title: The Unburden Race

itemAlts.name: Psychic Seed

itemAlts.name: White Herb

Enter after Boom sets terrain or on terrain already up.
Pop → SD or attack.

modes.label: Psychic Unburden

modes.objective: Race under Psychic terrain or on Seed entry.

moves.name: Swords Dance

packs.label: Anti-HO
packs.when: HO-shaped sixes — Golisopod, Sash, glass, early KOs.
packs.identity: Disguise + Glide + Primarina Jet — deny free turns. No Mega Chomp lead into revenge chains.

strategy.opponentPattern: Hyper Offense or fragile Balance that wins by taking free turns.
strategy.purpose: Disguise eats the opener; Glide and Jet finish.
refuses: Fat Fairy walls that laugh at Disguise
strategy.winCondition: Disguise / Knock chip into Glide, Shadow Sneak, or Aqua Jet.

pilot.rule: Disguise is one hit — spend it.
pilot.fail: Leading Mega Chomp into their revenge chain.

flows.title: Lead
flows.lede: Disguise frail openers; Boom when Knock/Glide is needed day one.

forks.when: Frail lead or likely First Impression.
Costume breaks and they cannot punish.

forks.why: Hold Dragons off the HO core.

forks.then: Play Rough or Shadow Sneak — do not soft.

flows.title: Late
flows.lede: Priority cascade — Sneak, Glide, Jet. No Mega Dance.

packs.label: Maximum pressure
packs.when: Passive sixes; you accept less glue for three offensive axes.
packs.identity: Scarf Chomp revenge + Unburden Sneasler + Mimikyu Disguise — continuous offense.

strategy.opponentPattern: Passive or slow sixes that lose to continuous offense.
strategy.purpose: Aggressive bring — Scarf cleans while Mimikyu or Sneasler sets up.
strategy.winCondition: Disguise or Seed window into Scarf cleanup.

pilot.thesis: Offense over glue — only when their six cannot punish Fairy holes.
pilot.rule: Scarf cleans; don’t SD Scarf. One setup piece at a time.
pilot.fail: Playing this like the Primarina balance package.

loops.title: Disguise → Scarf clean
loops.body: Mimikyu eats one; Scarf Chomp revenge.

loops.title: Seed → SD → Scarf
loops.body: Sneasler boosts; Scarf cleans the answer.

flows.title: Lead
flows.lede: Guaranteed action or Seed pressure — Scarf is usually the mid cleaner.

forks.when: Need a guaranteed action into their lead.
Speed control is the preview plan.
forks.then: Keep Scarf Chomp as revenge; chip with Mimikyu/Sneasler first.
forks.why: Scarf is the cleaner, not always the lead.

flows.title: Mid
flows.lede: One setup path — Disguise SD or Unburden SD — then Scarf.

forks.then: Mimikyu SD — do not also soft SD Sneasler.

forks.when: Seed popped and Mimikyu is not the setup.
They send into Disguise or a weakened name.

flows.title: Late
flows.lede: Scarf, Shadow Sneak, or Unburden CC.

packs.label: Steel crack
packs.identity: Sneasler CC + Boom Knock/Glide + Primarina — no Chomp required.

strategy.opponentPattern: Stamina / Leftovers Steel and Archaludon-shaped structures.
strategy.purpose: Knock strips; Close Combat cracks; Glide races; Primarina covers Dragons.
refuses: Pure Fairy offense with no Steel to crack
strategy.winCondition: Knock stripped → CC / Glide while Encore denies Protect.

pilot.thesis: Chomp EQ alone stalls Stamina — bring the Fighting/Grass axes.
pilot.rule: Knock first when Leftovers/Stamina items matter.
pilot.fail: Forcing Mega Chomp into Electro Shot rain without Boom/Sneasler.

loops.title: Encore → Unburden SD
loops.body: Primarina locks; Sneasler converts under terrain.

forks.when: Fighting is free on the lead.
Dragon / Fire support is the real problem.

flows.title: Mid
flows.lede: After Knock, CC and Glide; Encore Protect.

forks.why: Do not let Stamina rebuild the game.

flows.title: Late
flows.lede: Unburden CC, Glide, Moonblast — Chomp never needed.
